problem: The sentence 'It is threshold-free but still ignores class balance in the training data' attributes the weakness to the wrong place. AUC is computed from predicted scores on test items, and its known weakness is that it is insensitive to class imbalance — a model can score a high AUC while still missing most of the rare class. Training-set balance is not what AUC 'ignores'.
fix: ROC-AUC is threshold-free and insensitive to class imbalance: a high AUC is possible even when the model misses most of the rare class. For imbalanced problems, also report PR-AUC or precision at a fixed recall.

problem: 'A 90/10 imbalance makes micro close to accuracy' understates it. In single-label classification (each document has exactly one class) micro-averaged precision, recall and F1 are all exactly equal to accuracy, so micro gives no extra information under imbalance.
fix: In single-label classification, micro-averaged precision, recall and F1 all equal accuracy exactly, so micro hides the rare class completely; use macro or per-class scores to see it.

problem: The chi-square test is quoted without its validity condition. On a 2×2 table built from a rare word, expected counts fall below about 5 and the χ² value becomes unreliable, which is exactly the case for the rare features feature selection is meant to filter.
fix: Add: use χ² only when every expected count E is at least about 5; for very rare words the test is unreliable, so fall back on simple frequency counts or mutual information with smoothing.

problem: '20 false spam' is ambiguous — it can be read as 20 spam messages that are false, whereas the cell is 20 ham emails wrongly marked spam.
fix: A two-by-two confusion matrix: 80 true positives (spam caught), 20 false positives (ham marked spam), 10 false negatives (spam missed), 890 true negatives (ham correctly left alone).

problem: 'See 5.1.' is plain text; in this book cross-references are links, so the reader on a phone cannot jump to the earlier chapter.
fix: Make it a chapter link using the 5.1 chapter id, e.g. See 5.1.
